summary: Conversational handshake latency after runtime bridge and model roll-forward
description: Customer reports a sustained increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions immediately after the runtime 2.1.0 bridge and a model revision roll-forward to rwd-v2-pp. The issue manifests as a 300-1500ms additional delay before the first chunk is streamed in interactive sessions; subsequent token throughput is normal. Affects multiple customer sessions and elevated request timeouts for some long-prompt chats.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On dedicated cluster in us-east, pin runtime 2.1.0 and model rwd-v2-pp-rev3
2) Start a new chat session with a 250-400 token system+user prompt (interactive streaming enabled)
3) Observe the initial streaming handshake and measure TTFB (time until first chunk arrives)
4) Repeat across several instances to reproduce variability; compare against sessions pinned to runtime 2.0.3 + rwd-v2-large
logs: Customer-provided curl: POST /v1/chat/completions -> request_id: cst-92b1, latency: 1324ms to first chunk, 3xx total tokens streamed
Proxy logs (elb-us-east-3): 2026-03-10T14:07:22Z request_id=cst-92b1 upstream_connect_time=0.026 upstream_response_time=1.31 status=200
Serving node logs (node-rt-7): runtime-init: model_load=0.28s kernel_probe=0.41s compile_sync_block=1.02s trace=alloc_sync()
Prometheus snapshot (us-east): inference_start_latency_seconds{quantile="0.99"} increased from 0.45 -> 1.8 between 2026-03-09T23:00 and 2026-03-10T02:00
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Pattern correlated with runtime 2.1.0 bridge rollout and model revision that uses new kernel selection paths.
Hypothesis A: Synchronous graph/kernel compilation on first client request introduced blocking on the serving thread (evidence: compile_sync_block entry in node logs).
Hypothesis B: Scheduler affinity change caused cross-node routing that added an extra network hop (evidence: sporadic upstream_connect_time spikes in ELB logs for affected requests).
Collected metrics: increased 95/99p TTFB for chat-start spans, no corresponding increase in per-token generation time once streaming begins.
Reproduced internally on staging by forcing runtime 2.1.0 + rwd-v2-pp; median handshake latency rose ~450ms vs 2.0.3 baseline.
Node-level trace shows: model load path now triggers deferred kernel prefetch only after first request; a recent allocator change caused compile to run inline when prefetch misses occur.
Related code: runtime change introduced in github.com/redwood-inference/runtime@commit a7c3f9d and PR #4589 altered allocator behavior and compile blocking semantics.
Linked internal ticket INT-33412 opened to coordinate hotfix and infra rollout.
Customer impact: Several BrightLens AI streaming-only chat flows hit client-side 2s timeouts and saw degraded UX; no token corruption or wrong outputs observed.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Luis Ortega): Acknowledged to customer, requested request_ids, sample prompts and worst-affected session timestamps; escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10 - SRE (Hannah Park): Identified compile_sync_block events on node logs matching customer request_ids; marked as likely root cause and started rollback plan for allocator change.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Maya Patel): Prepared runtime 2.1.1 hotfix that defers kernel compilation off request thread and adds a pre-warm path during model activation; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621.

2026-03-11 - Support (Luis Ortega): Applied temporary mitigation by pinning affected customer's routes to runtime 2.0.3 and model rwd-v2-large; customer reported immediate improvement in handshake latency.
2026-03-12 - SRE (Hannah Park): Deployed 2.1.1 to us-east canary, monitored TTFB 99p drop from ~1.8s to ~0.48s across canary traffic; scheduled full rollout.

2026-03-12 - Customer (BrightLens AI - Alex Kim): Confirmed that pinned route restored expected behavior and that post-hotfix testing showed improved TTFB; closing the ticket after stabilization period.
resolution: Hotfix deployed in runtime 2.1.1 that defers kernel compilation off the serving request path and adds proactive kernel prefetch during model activation. Immediate customer mitigation: pinned their routes to runtime 2.0.3 until canary and full rollout validated. Monitoring shows TTFB back to baseline in us-east. Follow-up: revert allocator synchronous compile default and add a pre-warm CI test for handshake latency.
